name: Sharpe's Longclaw
rangeDescription: Grassy highlands of kenya
description: A small, pretty member of the pipit family. Note the yellow underparts, the breast band of black streaks, and the scaly brown upperparts.

name: Violet-eared Waxbill
rangeDescription: Angola to namibia, zambia, southern zimbabwe, botswana, and northern south africa
description: A stunning long-tailed waxbill with a red bill, mauve cheeks, and a blue rump. The underparts are vibrant chestnut in the male and cream-buff in the female.

name: Mexican Woodnymph
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of western mexico (southern nayarit, jalisco, and guerrero)
description: Very local in tropical foothills of west Mexico; endemic. Favors oak woodland and shade-coffee plantations.

name: Tricolored Blackbird
rangeDescription: Marshes and farmlands of southwestern oregon to northwestern baja california
description: Very similar to Red-winged Blackbird. Male entirely glossy black with red shoulder patch bordered by white, not yellow.

name: Heuglin's Wheatear
rangeDescription: Mauritania to mali, cameroon, sudan, ethiopia, and northwestern kenya
description: A brownish wheatear with a rusty breast. Note the white eyebrow, dark mask, and pale throat.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Gyrfalcon
rangeDescription: Mountains and tundra of northern palearctic region and northern north america
description: Stocky beast of a falcon; ranges in color from strikingly white to silvery-gray to dark sooty-brown. Relatively long tail and broad wings with powerful flight.

name: Baikal Teal
rangeDescription: Breeds in northern and eastern siberia; winters japan, korea, and eastern china
description: Males is exquisitely patterned, with an unmistakable green-and-yellow facial pattern, spotted rose-pink breast, and long, drooping scapulars. Female mostly drab brown but with a distinct white spot near the bill base as well as a very weak hint of the male's facial pattern.

name: Rufous-webbed Brilliant
rangeDescription: Andean foothills of eastern peru and (?) northwestern bolivia
description: Large, green hummingbird of montane forest. Males have a small red throat patch; females are duller green with a white-speckled belly.

name: Pectoral Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds arctic north america and siberia; winters to southern south america, australia
description: Beefy, medium-sized sandpiper. Brown-toned overall with yellowish legs.

name: Yellow-lored Tanager
rangeDescription: Tropical southern colombia to central bolivia (la paz eastward to western santa cruz)
description: Large and chunky with stout dark bill. Nondescript plumage: entirely olive-green with slightly brighter yellowish throat and upper breast.

name: Chestnut Bunting
rangeDescription: Siberia to northern mongolia and northeastern china; winters to india and southeastern asia
description: Small, shy bunting, usually seen through a screen of thick shrubby vegetation in low, dense thickets. Brightly colored adult male distinctive, with brilliant chestnut upperparts and a daisy-yellow belly.

name: Blue-capped Motmot
rangeDescription: Northeastern mexico (nuevo león and tamaulipas to northern veracruz)
description: Large motmot of humid forest and edge in tropical lowlands and foothills of northeast Mexico. Perches at all levels, usually in shady areas.

name: Jamaican Tody
rangeDescription: Hills and mountains of jamaica
description: A small, gemlike, woodland species usually found in pairs. Its rather large head, long bill, and short tail create a unique profile.

name: Red-shouldered Vanga
rangeDescription: Southwestern desert of madagascar
description: Small vanga that is built like a chickadee or tit. Male is colorful and female plain brownish.

name: Black-capped Rufous-Warbler
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to southeastern guinea, liberia, ivory coast, and ghana
description: Unusual and handsome forest-dwelling warbler. Mostly rufous-brown, with a black head and a black stripe onto the center of the belly.

name: Alström's Warbler
rangeDescription: Western and southern china; winters to thailand, cambodia, and northern vietnam
description: Sprightly, small warbler that poses a bevy of identification issues. Dull olive above and yellow below, with a bright eyering and a gray crown bound in by black stripes.

name: Caspian Plover
rangeDescription: Caspian sea to far western china; winters in eastern and southern africa
description: Stately plover with a gentle, dovelike expression. Breeding male is stunning, with a white face and belly separated by a broad chestnut patch across the chest.

name: Hudson's Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Central argentina; winters to bolivia, southwestern brazil, and southeastern peru
description: Highly migratory flycatcher that breeds in central Argentina from around September through March, then disperses north to Bolivia and Paraguay, and occasionally wanders even farther. Male is glossy black with a silvery, black-tipped bill.

name: Hume's Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Himalayas of northern india, nepal, bhutan, and southeastern tibet
description: This dull, shy skulker can be difficult to see; instead, listen for its remarkable song, an ascending series of 3-4 long thin monotone whistles (“doooooo-rayyyyy-meeeee”) followed by a slow series of repeated 2- or 3-note musical phrases. If seen well, note the species’ white brow stripe, buff-washed pale underparts, and warm brown upperparts.

name: Crow-billed Drongo
rangeDescription: Eastern himalayas to southern china; winters to southeastern asia and greater sundas
description: Large dark drongo of open forested environments. Glossy black with a characteristically forked tail.
